headline: Revenue and earnings decline year over year as costs climb
summary_short: Revenue of $256M fell 3.8% y/y but rose 7.1% q/q; net income of $18M dropped 48.6% y/y despite a 12.5% q/q gain, as rising stock-based compensation, technology, and SG&A costs pushed operating margin down to 11.7% (-10.1ppt y/y).
summary_long: Revenue fell 3.8% y/y to $256M as consumer data and video revenue declined (video services were discontinued in 2025), though it rose 7.1% q/q. Higher stock-based compensation, technology, SG&A, and Quintillion-acquisition costs pushed operating income down to $30M (-48.3% y/y, -6.3% q/q); Adjusted OIBDA fell $20M y/y. Net income dropped to $18M (-48.6% y/y) but rose 12.5% q/q on lower interest expense and higher interest income from the November 2025 rights offering. Cash rose to $435M (+4.6% q/q) after the rights-offering proceeds; long-term debt was roughly flat at $981M; equity grew to $1,712M (+18.1% y/y). No share repurchases this quarter; no quantified forward guidance given.

drivers.explanation: Consumer data revenue fell on subscriber losses and the 2025 exit from video service; consumer wireless grew on subscriber gains; business data fell against a one-time prior-year healthcare rate-appeal benefit.
Consumer direct costs fell on the video-service exit, but business direct costs rose on healthcare/education distribution costs, against a smaller revenue base overall.
Revenue fell while business direct costs rose, mechanically compressing the gross-profit-to-revenue ratio despite consumer cost savings.

Higher stock-based compensation (grant-timing shift), technology expense, SG&A, and Quintillion acquisition costs outweighed lower consumer direct costs; filing states operating income "was impacted by the above explanations."
Operating expenses grew faster than revenue on the cost items above, mechanically lowering the operating-income-to-revenue ratio.
Company-disclosed Adjusted OIBDA fell $20M y/y "due to the items discussed above" — the same stock comp, technology, SG&A and acquisition-cost increases cited for operating income.

Filing attributes the net-earnings change to "the above-described fluctuations in our revenue, expenses, and other income and expenses," partly offset by lower interest expense and higher interest income from rights-offering cash.
Mechanical consequence of net income falling faster than revenue year over year; not separately addressed in the release.
Tracks the net-income decline; share count was little changed this quarter versus the year-ago period.
Filing states the decrease "was primarily driven by decreased net earnings and timing differences in working capital accounts."

Cash equivalents remain elevated following the November 2025 rights offering, which raised approximately $300 million; the filing notes $316 million of related cash equivalents on hand at quarter-end.

Consolidated revenue and operating income both declined versus the year-ago quarter on video-service exit and higher stock comp/technology/SG&A/acquisition costs, partly offset by wireless subscriber growth and rights-offering interest income.
